newsitem.title: RWANDA: Three killed in raid on Rwandan hospital.
newsitem.headline: Three killed in raid on Rwandan hospital.

text.p: Three Rwandan civilians were shot dead and three others wounded when 60 suspected Rwandan Hutu militiamen attacked a hospital in northwestern Rwanda on Saturday night, aid officials said on Monday.
"It was a very violent attack," Muriel Cornelius, coordinator of the medical Medecins Sans Frontieres-Belgium (MSF-Belgium), told Reuters in the capital Kigali.

"Our staff counted around 60 attackers who shot the six people around the hospital. They looted and stole medical supplies, making us think they either had wounded nearby in the Gishwati forest or were stockpiling supplies," Cornelius added.
Kabaya lies 80 km (50 miles) from Kigali on the northeast edge of Gishwati forest, a favoured refuge for Interahamwe militiamen infiltrating into Rwanda from Zaire.
Cornelius said the attackers told two MSF doctors "exactly how they were going to be killed, and what they were going to do with them" before stealing watches and radios.
One of the wounded was brought to Kigali for treatment after being paralysed in the attack.

The 100-bed hospital lies close to Giciye, a hardline Hutu stronghold and hometown of ex-president Juvenal Habyarimana, whose death in a plane-crash over Kigali in April 1994 sparked the genocide in which an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and moderate Hutus were slaughtered by the Hutu army, militias and mobs.
Since more than a million refugees were forced home late last year from camps in Tanzania and Zaire, the problem of armed incursions across Rwanda's borders has continued.
"What we are experiencing is infiltrators inside Rwanda attempting destabilisation to prove they still exist," said Rwandan military spokesman Major Emmanuel Ndahiro recently.

Last week's ambush of two minibuses near the deserted refugee camp of Katale 48 km (30 miles) north of Goma by suspected Hutu militiamen has increased the belief that Rwandan-backed Zairean Tutsi rebels are overstretched and losing control around the border area.
Aid workers and Rwandan military officials said last week that up to 50 people had been killed in incidents involving infiltrators since Christmas.
